items.title: Lou Donaldson — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: Any time I talked to him, he’d come up and we’d talk.

ctx.x: You could separate your feelings in that regard.

Oh, yeah. I’m an amazing guy, because I’m the only guy... Say, like, a guy like Miles... Miles did some bad things to people. He never did it to me. Any time I talked to him, he’d come up and we’d talk. Monk. Monk would hardly talk to people. People asked Monk, said, “How you doing, Monk?” He’d just look at them. He wouldn’t say a word. Every time I saw him, we’d talk. We’d talk a long time. We were very friendly. In fact, I used to really feel sorry for Monk, because back then, his music wasn’t compatible. I…

coming up to 110th Street, Central Park, and I stopped at a light. They said, “Wait a minute. I got to get out, I got to get out.” So I thought he was going out there to take a leak or something. So he comes back and opens the back door, and I hear this noise back there, CLING-A-LING-A­ LING-A-LING. So I took back there. Four hubcaps. [LAUGHS] I said, “Man, are you crazy?! Not only... You weren’t out there but a few seconds. Where did you get four hubcaps?” You know what he had? He had a can opener.
